creator.label: Who's behind it
creator.bio: Hey, I'm Alberto Dumontt. I built dev for devs because I was missing a real support space for developers — no paywall, no empty promises — where it's possible to grow together, ask real questions, and find guidance from people who've faced the same challenges. This isn't a product: it's a community being built. If you're a dev and want to contribute, you're welcome here.

index.title: Roadmaps
index.subtitle: Study paths curated by community professionals. Each roadmap is a real recommendation, based on hands-on experience.

backendBeginner.cardDesc: Backend development fundamentals: logic, language, databases, REST APIs, and deployment.
backendBeginner.title: Backend for Beginners
backendBeginner.subtitle: A practical, step-by-step guide for anyone starting out in backend development. Follow the steps in order, without rushing — consistency is worth more than speed.
backendBeginner.recommenterBio: Focused on backend, REST APIs, and system architecture, Alberto believes learning is consolidated through practice — building real projects, making mistakes, adjusting, and evolving. This roadmap reflects the path he took and recommends for those just starting out.

projectIdeas.title: Project Ideas
projectIdeas.subtitle: Projects suggested by Alberto Dumontt — out of the ordinary, designed to consolidate what you've learned with real challenges.

items.title: Banking System with OOP
items.desc: Build a banking system from scratch. Create classes like Account, CheckingAccount, SavingsAccount, and Client, applying inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism. Add real rules: overdraft limits, savings interest, and transaction history. You'll truly understand OOP when you have to model something with real business logic — not a textbook example, but a system that actually works.

items.title: REST API with Layered Architecture
items.desc: Build a management API (personal finance, inventory, or tasks) applying separation of concerns: Controller receives the request, Service executes business logic, Repository talks to the database. Add JWT authentication and input validation. This is the project that simulates a real work environment — and one you'll actually be able to show in interviews.

steps.title: Programming Logic
steps.desc: Before any language, learn to think like a programmer: variables, conditionals, loops, functions, and basic data structures. This is the foundation of everything — without it, any language will feel like magic.

steps.title: Pick Your First Language
steps.desc: Choose one language and go deep. Alongside the syntax, learn the two pillars that define how you'll think and write professional code: Data Structures (lists, stacks, queues, maps) and Object-Oriented Programming — classes, inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism. Don't move on without understanding these concepts.

steps.title: Git & Version Control
steps.desc: Learn Git from your very first project. Know how to commit, push, pull, create branches, and resolve conflicts. Use GitHub to store and showcase your work — it's your real portfolio.

steps.title: Relational Databases
steps.desc: Learn real SQL: create tables, insert, update, delete, and query data with filters, joins, and groupings. Understand relationships (1:1, 1:N, N:M) and how to model a database from scratch.

steps.title: Build Your First REST API
steps.desc: Understand HTTP in practice — verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), status codes, and JSON. Build an API with real endpoints using your language's framework. Test it with Postman or Insomnia.

steps.title: Authentication & Basic Security
steps.desc: Learn to protect your API: authenticate users with JWT, hash passwords with bcrypt, and never store sensitive data as plain text. Security isn't optional — it starts at your first endpoint.

steps.title: Deploy — Go Live
steps.desc: Put your API on the internet. Learn about environment variables, how to use free platforms, and the basics of a deploy flow. A project nobody can access doesn't exist.
